newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Czech unemployment unlikely to top 4 pct -CNB head.
newsitem.headline: Czech unemployment unlikely to top 4 pct -CNB head.

text.p: Unemployment in the Czech Republic should not exceed four percent in the near future, Czech National Bank Josef Tosovsky said on Monday in a speech prepared for delivery in Pretoria.
The jobless rate rose to four percent in January from 3.5 percent in December, according to figures released last week.

But the central bank head argued unemployment would be capped by the creation of jobs in the service sector and the strength of the private sector, which now accounts for 75 percent of the economy against only three percent six years ago.

"Unemployment has been kept low during the whole transformantion period, thanks mainly to the rapid emergence of new private firms, and a large shift of labour into the previously underdeveloped service sector," Tosovsky said in his speech to an audience at the South African Reserve Bank.
"Even with microeconomic restructuring going on, unemployment is not expected to exceed a four percent level in the near future."
Tosovsky said the Czech Republic had made good progress in fighting inflation but he reiterated that the goal was to drive the rate down further in future.
"(The) inflation rate has been put under control and reduced to one digit rate, 8.9 percent in 1996, and it is our ambition to reduce it further down to 4-5 percent within the next few years."
The year-on-year rate of increase in consumer prices stood at 7.4 percent in January 1997 from 9.0 percent in January 1996.
